title: C2. Yet Another Nim Game (Counting version)

legend: Alice and Bob decided to play the following game on n%%ZSMJ0%% piles of stones where the ith(1≤i≤n)%%ZSMJ1%% pile contains pi%%ZSMJ2%% stones, with Alice starting first :

On his/her turn, he/she will choose any k(1≤k≤n)%%ZSMJ3%% distinct arbitrary piles which have a positive number of stones(note that k%%ZSMJ4%% can be chosen arbitrarily by the current player). Now the player will remove exactly one stone each from all selected k%%ZSMJ5%% piles.
The player who cannot make a move loses. Note that both Alice and Bob are intelligent, so they always play optimally.

Now your task is to count the number of permutations†%%ZSMJ6%% p%%ZSMJ7%% of length n%%ZSMJ8%% such that the number of pairs (l,r%%ZSMJ9%%)(1≤l≤r≤n%%ZSMJ10%%), where Alice will win if both players play the game on piles l,l+1,...,r−1,r%%ZSMJ11%%, is maximum possible.
†%%ZSMJ12%% A permutation is an array of length n%%ZSMJ13%%, where each number from 1%%ZSMJ14%% to n%%ZSMJ15%% appears exactly once.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ16%% (1≤t≤10000%%ZSMJ17%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤n≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ19%%) — the number of piles.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ20%% over all test cases doesn't exceed 3⋅105%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: For each test case, print a single integer — the required answer modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ22%%.
